_purpose: Every JUDGMENT call (things a human or source-code — not a mechanical rule — decided): story splits, priority, scope in/out, how a PENDING item was resolved, spec-vs-code policy. Converts silent judgment into an owned, queryable record.
_why: A mechanical run can assemble schema + traceability on its own. It must NOT silently pick a side on a judgment call. This ledger is the HALT-and-flag surface: an autonomous run stops on any open human decision instead of guessing.

type_vocab.split: re-decompose a story into QA-internal units
type_vocab.pending-resolution: how a PENDING clarification was answered (PM round OR source code)
type_vocab.spec-correction: spec deliberately differs from the Jira/PM wording
type_vocab.policy: cross-cutting rule for how the spec itself is authored / the pipeline is run

status_vocab.resolved-by-code: answered from source code with a file ref — settled (no PM round needed)
status_vocab.proposed: QA proposed it; awaiting human confirmation — OPEN
status_vocab.pending-human: explicitly needs a named owner to sign off — OPEN

_halt_rule: AUTONOMOUS run must HALT if any decision of type {split, priority, scope, policy} has status {proposed, pending-human}, OR any {pending-resolution} lacks a source_ref. {confirmed} and {resolved-by-code with source_ref} are settled and do not block. Enforced by checks/decision_ledger.py --autonomous.

decisions.decision: The 4 UC1 platform stories (PDT-3675 Core API, PDT-3724 Android UIKit, PDT-3725 iOS UIKit, PDT-3726 React/Web UIKit) carry BYTE-IDENTICAL acceptance criteria (5 scenarios). Author them as ONE canonical UC1 unit (5 ac_id, keyed PDT-3675). Analysis / scenarios / test cases are authored ONCE against the 5 AC. Platform-specific differences (event-type chip + community-avatar + dark-theme rendering, client-side date/time formatting, API payload vs UIKit render, deep-link) are captured as platform NOTES and — where a divergence is confirmed real, not a bug — R3 platform-behavior-registry entries; NOT as duplicated per-platform AC. Manifest = 5 ac_id.
decisions.rationale: AC identical across all 4 clones (verified via Atlassian MCP 2026-07-14). Splitting into 4×5=20 ac_id would 4× the coverage burden with zero added behavioural signal. Platform differences are test-focus/rendering, not AC. Mirrors the PDT-3418 per-UC (not per-platform) structure.

decisions.decision: event_created tray audience = ALL active, non-banned NETWORK users on a PUBLIC community event (incl. non-members of that community); PRIVATE = members only. Audience is a SNAPSHOT at send time (no recompute on privacy change); public→private privacy exposure handled by the navigation/permission layer, not by revoking items. Tray is intentionally network-wide while push is NOT (TR-CL-02).
decisions.rationale: PM answers TR-CL-07 ('All members of the network') + TR-CL-16 ('does not recompute … navigation should already handle it') + TR-CL-02 (intentional tray/push asymmetry). TR-CL-16 corroborates the network-wide reading. Consequence: user story persona 'As a community member' is too narrow and must be updated in Jira (FU-3).
decisions.source_ref: user 2026-07-16 (PM answers in chat); qa/PDT-3421/1_clarifications.json TR-CL-07/16/02
decisions._confirmed: 2026-07-16 — user confirmed 'members of the network' = all users incl. community non-members. Network-wide locked, no wording ambiguity remaining.

decisions.decision: The comprehensive MANUAL test suite covers BOTH the Notification Tray (PDT-3421 UC1 = PDT-3675, 5 AC; clients Web+iOS+Android) AND Push Notification (cross-epic PDT-3420: UC1 console config = PDT-3676, 3 AC [Admin Console + backend]; UC2 member receive+navigate = PDT-3677, 5 AC [mobile iOS/Android + backend]). Total manifest = 13 AC. Push stories are Deployed to Staging (testable). Web receives NO device push (push = mobile OS notification) -> push client coverage = iOS+Android; console coverage = web console.
decisions.rationale: User chose scope 'UC1 tray + push (PDT-3420)' (AskUserQuestion 2026-07-16). Push shares the same event, nav (jack: 'reuse navigation from noti tray'), timezone rule, deleted-event handling, and content pattern as the tray -> one coherent suite. Push introduces NO new hard blocker: audience=community members (network toggle held/out), tz=event-tz (same PM rule), deleted->404, virtual->single push (Room go-live suppressed), OS-opt-out independent of tray.

decisions.decision: QA expected-result for the event-type chip (TR-CL-21): assert LEGIBILITY (sufficient text/background contrast) in BOTH light and dark theme on each platform; accept per-platform styling divergence as long as legible. Do NOT require pixel-identical cross-platform chip. Android light-theme white-on-white FAILS = BUG-D (to file).
decisions.rationale: User decided 2026-07-16 (AskUserQuestion: Chip theme) - 'legible both themes is enough; divergence OK; Android light = BUG-D'. Lets QA author the chip test cases now without waiting on a Design color spec (non-blocking Design nicety).

decisions.decision: REVERSAL of the TR-CL-05 timezone decision. The notification tray shows the event start date/time in the VIEWER's LOCAL (device) timezone, following existing UIKit behavior (event cards + event detail pages already display local time). Explicitly NOT a new timezone feature. Supersedes the earlier 'follow the event timezone' answer + the NY/Bangkok event-tz example. Consequence: the client's current device-local formatting is CORRECT -> BUG-B1 RETRACTED. Push (server-rendered OS text, PDT-3420/BUG-B2) was NOT covered by the dev statement (viewer-local not feasible server-side) -> push display timezone is re-opened, needs a separate product decision.
decisions.rationale: Developer feedback relayed by user 2026-07-21: tray start time should follow existing UIKit behavior = viewer's local timezone; 'should not be treated as a new timezone decision' since event cards / detail already show local. PM accepted, reversing the prior TR-CL-05 resolution.
decisions.source_ref: user 2026-07-21 (relaying PM reversal + dev statement); supersedes 1_clarifications.json TR-CL-05 (2026-07-16)
decisions._followup_2026_07_21: Later same day: QA verified on Android + iOS that PUSH also renders device-local (viewer-local) correctly — consistent with the tray. Push display-tz question RESOLVED (device-local, not re-opened after all); BUG-B2 RETRACTED (the source-based UTC inference did not reproduce on device).

decisions.decision: The enriched event-created tray notification (new rich copy: avatar+chip+date/time, AND the AC-04/05 network-wide-for-public-communities audience logic) applies ONLY to events created ON/AFTER this release's ship date. Events created before the release are excluded entirely from this feature — no retroactive re-skinning with new copy, no retroactive network-wide reach. This SUPERSEDES the earlier as-built-only finding for TR-CL-13 (which found old items DO get new copy at read time, with no release-date gate) — that was a description of current code behavior, not a confirmed requirement.
decisions.rationale: User decided directly 2026-07-21 while simplifying the '[ Backfill & old format ]' manual test case: a clean cutover is simpler to reason about and test than re-skinning historical data, and avoids the exact confusion TR-CL-26 raised (old events looking freshly-enriched is surprising). Also makes the scenario naturally untestable-going-forward once shipped (every event you can manually test after the cutoff is, by definition, post-release).
decisions.source_ref: user 2026-07-21 (chat); supersedes TR-CL-13 as-built finding + TR-CL-26
decisions._engineering_note: SUPERSEDED — see _amended_2026_07_22. No cutoff/guard needed after all.
decisions._amended_2026_07_22: PARTIALLY REVERSED per TR-CL-30 (PM follow-up, answer C): the COPY dimension is NOT excluded for pre-release events after all — an existing user's already-delivered old-format tray item (within the 30-day retention window) DOES get re-skinned with the new rich copy when reopened, matching the original TR-CL-13 as-built default. This reverses this decision's 'no retroactive re-skinning with new copy' clause. The AUDIENCE dimension is unaffected and still holds — old events remain community-scoped (they were created before the network-wide-audience code existed, so audienceScope=NETWORK was never structurally possible for them). CORRECTION to the engineering note below: NO new engineering guard is needed for EITHER dimension — copy already renders fresh at read time (confirmed correct), and audience scope is already naturally forward-only per-record (nothing to retroactively change). Net: this decision required zero engineering work, not the cutoff originally assumed.

decisions.decision: User-level blocking (bidirectional, same as other content types) is extended to cover community events: (A) a block made AFTER an event notification was already delivered blocks the recipient's TAP access (no-access state), (B) a block made BEFORE event creation suppresses the notification entirely (already covered by the existing audience-exclusion behavior), (C) blocked users don't see each other's events in the Event Hub / Event tab listing either.
decisions.rationale: Eng (Jack) confirmed 2026-07-21: 'this was not originally considered as part of scope but needs to be added' — extending the existing bidirectional content-blocking rule to events for consistency.
